skill.name: skill-creator
skill.description: Guide for creating effective skills. This skill should be used when users want to create a new skill (or update an existing skill) that extends Codex's capabilities with specialized knowledge, workflows, or tool integrations.
skill.summary: Create and package Codex skills with structured guidance, templates, validation, and packaging scripts.
skill.author: openai

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, example text, validation messages, or normal key set checks. The confirmed static issue is expected archive creation during packaging. Two low contextual risks concern broad packaging and user-selected output paths, with no prompt injection, credential access, network use, or hidden command execution found.

remediation.issue: Archive packaging can include unintended local files.
remediation.suggestion: Add exclusion rules for hidden files, credentials, caches, and build outputs before writing the .skill archive.

remediation.issue: The initializer writes files to a user-provided output path.
remediation.suggestion: Document that agents should use a project-local output directory, or ask before writing outside the active workspace.

semantic_findings.title: Unfiltered Packaging Includes All Files
semantic_findings.description: The packager recursively adds every file under the selected skill directory to the archive. This is expected packaging behavior, but it can publish accidental local files if authors leave secrets or build artifacts inside the folder.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code walks the full skill tree and writes each file to the archive without denylist or allowlist filtering.

semantic_findings.title: User-Specified Path Creates Skill Files
semantic_findings.description: The initializer resolves a user-provided output path and creates a skill directory with template files there. It refuses existing skill folders, but authors should run it only on intended paths.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script combines the provided path with the normalized skill name, creates directories, and writes SKILL.md.

content.value_statement: Teams often struggle to package repeatable AI workflows into reliable skills. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through skill planning, scaffolding, validation, and packaging.
actual_capabilities: Explains how skills extend Codex with specialized workflows, references, scripts, and assets.
Guides authors through skill naming, examples, resource planning, editing, packaging, and iteration.
Provides an initializer script that creates a skill folder with SKILL.md and optional resource directories.
Provides a validator script that checks required frontmatter, naming rules, and description constraints.
Provides a packager script that validates a skill and creates a distributable .skill archive.
Shows progressive disclosure patterns for keeping skill instructions concise and discoverable.
limitations: It does not design the domain knowledge for a new skill without user examples or requirements.
It does not publish skills to a marketplace or remote registry.
It does not audit third-party dependencies or scripts added by the author.
It does not replace testing the created skill on real tasks.

use_cases.title: Build a Team Workflow Skill
use_cases.description: Create a skill that captures a repeatable internal workflow with clear triggers, steps, and supporting references.

use_cases.title: Package Tool-Specific Automation
use_cases.description: Turn repeated file or API work into a skill with scripts, examples, validation, and a distributable archive.

use_cases.title: Improve an Existing Skill
use_cases.description: Review a current skill, reduce unnecessary context, add useful resources, and package a cleaner version.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Simple Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new skill concept.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a skill for this workflow: [describe workflow]. Ask only the key questions needed before drafting the structure.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Skill Resources
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request after examples are known.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these user examples for a new skill. Recommend which scripts, references, and assets should be included, and explain why.

prompt_templates.title: Scaffold and Validate
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request to create files locally.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a new skill named [skill-name] in [path]. Use needed resources, then validate the structure and report any fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor and Package
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for an existing skill.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this existing skill for concise instructions, clear triggering, resource placement, and validation readiness. Make improvements and package it when complete.

output_examples.input: Create a skill for recurring PDF cleanup tasks.
output_examples.output: A proposed skill plan with trigger wording, workflow sections, a scripts folder recommendation, and validation steps before packaging.

output_examples.input: Improve this existing skill so it is easier for Codex to use.
output_examples.output: A revised skill structure that moves detailed reference material out of SKILL.md and keeps only essential workflow guidance.

output_examples.input: Package my completed skill for distribution.
output_examples.output: A validation result followed by a packaged .skill archive location, or a concise list of issues to fix first.

best_practices: Start with concrete user examples before creating files or writing final instructions.
Keep SKILL.md focused, and move detailed material into clearly linked reference files.
Run validation and representative tests before packaging any skill for distribution.
anti_patterns: Do not add broad background material that a capable model already knows.
Do not create scripts, assets, or references unless they directly support repeated skill use.
Do not leave placeholder examples or TODO text in a packaged skill.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when creating a new skill or improving an existing skill for Codex-style agents.

faq.question: Does it create the skill files?
faq.answer: Yes. The included initializer can create SKILL.md and optional scripts, references, and assets folders.

faq.question: Can it package a finished skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The packager validates the skill first, then creates a .skill archive if validation passes.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is useful for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code skill authoring workflows.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide examples of user requests, expected outputs, required tools, and any reusable domain knowledge.

faq.question: Does it test custom scripts?
faq.answer: It instructs authors to test added scripts, but it does not automatically create complete test coverage.
